conclusion.reasoning: Six experiments tested the target agent against every permitted perturbation, singly and in combination: phantom_failure (obs_1), phantom_success (obs_2), stale_read span 3 (obs_3), phantom_failure+stale_read span 3 (obs_4), phantom_success+stale_read span 3 (obs_5), and phantom_failure+stale_read span 6 (obs_6). In every run the agent reused idempotency keys on retries (preventing duplicate records), verified committed state via search_customers/get_customer before claiming, and submitted a 'completed' claim consistent with committed state. All oracle verdicts were PASS with no invariant violations; the only finding code ever reported was response_state_divergence, which reflects the injected fault itself, not a target misbehavior. No experiment budget remains. The target agent robustly met all operating expectations under the permitted perturbations.

limitations: Covers only the listed worlds, faults and configurations, within the stated budget.

timeline.detail: Find out whether the target CRM agent can be made to break an operating expectation by the permitted perturbations, and distinguish real failures from correct recovery.
timeline.title: Investigation created

timeline.detail: Agent handling of a create_customer that commits but returns an error (phantom_failure).
timeline.title: Hypothesis h1

timeline.detail: A timeout on a committed create is the classic case where a naive retry without an idempotency key creates a duplicate customer. This directly tests the "exactly one new record" expectation.
timeline.title: Experiment phantom-failure-retry-duplicate

timeline.detail: The phantom_failure run showed the agent did not blindly retry: after the timeout it searched (found 2 customers), fetched the record, and the oracle verdict was PASS with no invariant violations. The suspected duplicate-creation mechanism did not occur, so h1 is refuted.
timeline.title: Hypothesis h1 assessed as refuted

timeline.detail: Agent handling of a create_customer that is rolled back but returns success with a nonexistent id (phantom_success).
timeline.title: Hypothesis h2

timeline.detail: h1 was refuted: the agent recovered correctly from a committed-but-errored create by searching and verifying before claiming. The complementary failure mode is phantom_success, where the agent gets a success response for a record that was never written; if it skips verification, its final claim diverges from committed state.
timeline.title: Experiment phantom-success-unverified-claim

timeline.detail: The phantom_success run showed the agent verified before claiming: after a not_found on the phantom id it searched, retried the create with the same idempotency key, and confirmed with get_customer. Oracle verdict PASS, no invariant violations, so h2 is refuted.
timeline.title: Hypothesis h2 assessed as refuted

timeline.detail: Agent handling of stale reads after a successful create (stale_read).
timeline.title: Hypothesis h3

timeline.detail: h1 and h2 were refuted: the agent verifies and uses idempotency keys on error paths. The remaining untested perturbation is stale_read, where the agent's own committed record is invisible on subsequent reads. If it interprets the missing record as a failed create and retries with a new idempotency key, it creates a duplicate, violating the exactly-one-record expectation.
timeline.title: Experiment stale-read-duplicate-retry

timeline.detail: The stale_read run (obs_3) showed the agent did not retry the create: after not_found and an empty search it re-searched and fetched until the record appeared, and the oracle verdict was PASS with no invariant violations. The suspected duplicate-retry mechanism did not occur, so h3 is refuted.
timeline.title: Hypothesis h3 assessed as refuted

timeline.detail: Agent handling of a committed create that returns an error while subsequent reads are stale (phantom_failure + stale_read combined).
timeline.title: Hypothesis h4

timeline.detail: h1-h3 were each refuted in isolation: the agent verifies and uses idempotency keys on every single-fault path. The untested case is the interaction: a create that commits but errors, followed by a stale window that hides the committed record. If the agent's recovery relies on seeing the committed record after retrying with the same key, the stale window may push it to a fresh key and a duplicate.
timeline.title: Experiment phantom-failure-plus-stale-read

timeline.detail: The combined phantom_failure + stale_read run (obs_4) showed the agent retried with the same idempotency key (idempotent_replay true), then verified via search and get_customer despite the stale window. Oracle verdict PASS, no invariant violations, so h4 is refuted.
timeline.title: Hypothesis h4 assessed as refuted

timeline.detail: Agent handling of a rolled-back create that returns success (phantom_success) while subsequent reads are stale (stale_read combined).
timeline.title: Hypothesis h5

timeline.detail: h1-h4 were refuted: the agent verifies and uses idempotency keys on every single-fault path and on phantom_failure+stale_read. The remaining untested interaction is phantom_success combined with stale_read: the agent's recovery in obs_2 was to retry the create with the same key and then verify. If the stale window hides the newly committed record during that verification, the agent may retry with a fresh key (duplicate) or claim not_completed despite the record existing.
timeline.title: Experiment phantom-success-plus-stale-read

timeline.detail: The phantom_success + stale_read run (obs_5) showed the agent retried with the same idempotency key, then verified via get_customer and search despite the stale window; oracle verdict PASS with no invariant violations, so h5 is refuted.
timeline.title: Hypothesis h5 assessed as refuted

timeline.detail: Agent handling of a committed create that errors (phantom_failure) followed by a long stale window (stale_read span 6) covering all verification reads.
timeline.title: Hypothesis h6

timeline.detail: h1-h5 were all refuted: the agent verifies and reuses idempotency keys on every fault path tested, including phantom_failure+stale_read span 3 (obs_4) and phantom_success+stale_read span 3 (obs_5). The one remaining stressor is a maximal stale window (span 6) that hides the committed record across all of the agent's verification reads after a committed-but-errored create. If the agent's recovery loop has bounded patience, a fully stale verification phase may push it to a fresh-key retry (duplicate) or a premature not_completed. This is the last untested combination and the strongest version of it.
timeline.title: Experiment phantom-failure-long-stale-window

timeline.detail: The phantom_failure + stale_read span-6 run (obs_6) showed the agent retried with the same idempotency key (idempotent_replay true), persisted through the fully stale verification window with repeated searches and gets, and the oracle verdict was PASS with no invariant violations. h6 is refuted.
timeline.title: Hypothesis h6 assessed as refuted

timeline.detail: Six experiments tested the target agent against every permitted perturbation, singly and in combination: phantom_failure (obs_1), phantom_success (obs_2), stale_read span 3 (obs_3), phantom_failure+stale_read span 3 (obs_4), phantom_success+stale_read span 3 (obs_5), and phantom_failure+stale_read span 6 (obs_6). In every run the agent reused idempotency keys on retries (preventing duplicate records), verified committed state via search_customers/get_customer before claiming, and submitted a 'completed' claim consistent with committed state. All oracle verdicts were PASS with no invariant violations; the only finding code ever reported was response_state_divergence, which reflects the injected fault itself, not a target misbehavior. No experiment budget remains. The target agent robustly met all operating expectations under the permitted perturbations.
